schema_note: Rule registry for this session's half of the counseling-intelligence research package (branch oryn/counseling-intelligence-research-013956). The peer session's rules (on oryn/counseling-intelligence-research, docs 03/07/08/06-family-docs-01-through-09) live in a separate registry, NOT yet merged — see docs/handoffs/research-counseling-intelligence.md for the full topology and the one known direct ID collision (RULE-COUNSEL-056, minted independently by both branches for different rules). Do not treat this file as the complete package; it is one of two halves pending a coordinated final-integration renumbering pass.

rules.statement: Use the Common Data Set's 19-factor academic/nonacademic split as the reference vocabulary for whether a proposed evidence category is admissions-relevant.
Weight academic rigor/grades above any single extracurricular dimension when both compete for a student's limited time.
Never recommend an activity primarily because it 'looks impressive' rather than genuine interest or a genuine profile gap.
Default counseling posture should favor 1-3 sustained, meaningful commitments over many shallow ones.
Treat 'depth over breadth' as directional guidance, not a quantitative formula — never invent a specific 'ideal activity count'.
Do not treat 'no publication' as a research-dimension weakness on its own; mentored process/methodology/independence are legitimate strong evidence without output.
Redundancy/saturation logic must operate per-dimension, not per-activity — one activity legitimately scoring against multiple dimensions is correct, not double-counting.
Treat awards_distinction level-tier point values as unvalidated product heuristics, not research-backed precision.
A counselor should recognize when a student needs more breadth (exploration) rather than more depth, and recommend exploration without treating it as lower-value.
Achievement tier and verification status are independent axes; recommendation confidence should reflect the weaker of the two, never let a high tier claim substitute for low verification.
Do not phrase research-program recommendations as if publication is the expected outcome; frame the mentored process as complete evidence, output as a minority bonus.
Do not phrase competition recommendations as if placing/winning is the expected outcome, even for selective-final-round students.
Do not equate 'finalist'/'semifinalist' language with 'winner' language sharing the same geographic scope word — different tiers, should not score identically.
Evaluate founder/leadership-role attributes on any evidence item regardless of category, not only within nominally leadership/entrepreneurship categories.
Evaluate course rigor relative to what was actually offered to the student, mirroring the School Profile mechanism real admissions offices use.
ORYN's schema has no way to know what curriculum a student's school offers beyond what the student took — treat 'rigor relative to availability' as unresolvable with current data.
Default assumption for a thin activity profile should not be 'low effort' — access/quantity disparities by race and class are real and measurable; initiative within available activities is not.
A gap that cannot be confirmed as access-available should be presented as a hedged observation, never a flat deficiency claim.

Low execution_project_depth evidence for a stated technical interest is a clearer 'real gap' case since self-directed projects have a lower access bar — but must be framed as 'start something small,' never a capability deficit.
Never recommend a specific scarce/competitive pathway (e.g. student government) as THE fix for a leadership gap; recommend the underlying construct instead.
Never recommend 'take more advanced courses' without a hedge acknowledging availability cannot currently be verified.
Read gap severity in light of grade/stage context without altering the computed severity score itself.
Do not assume most students are over-scheduled; large-sample data suggests under-involvement is at least as common.
Do not assert activity intensity causes worse outcomes; at least one longitudinal study found the opposite direction.
Do not cite specific weekly-hour overscheduling thresholds as research-backed; untraceable to a primary source.
Ground 'don't add another activity in an already-strong area' in signal-quality-to-evaluators evidence, not wellbeing claims.
Ground the same recommendation in opportunity cost against the student's actual stated time budget wherever that data exists.
Redundancy strength should depend on tier relationship (escalation/lateral-repeat/level-mismatch/different-sub-skill/cross-dimension-reinforcement), not merely shared ProfileDimension.
Never explain an eligibility/deadline/cost/geography exclusion using redundancy or profile-strength language.
Distinguish 'not valuable' (redundancy/prestige-only) from 'not now' (time-budget/sequencing) in student-facing language.
An avoid_for_now explanation should be fully constructible from already-strong-dimension + tier-relationship + time-budget-opportunity-cost, no wellbeing claims.
Evaluate medicine-track evidence across three areas (clinical exposure, research, community involvement), emphasizing reflection/depth over raw hours.
Reframe undergraduate pre-med evidence guidance for ORYN's actual 14-18 population: shadowing/age-appropriate volunteering, not certified clinical employment.
Never cite MCAT/med-school-admission benchmarks to a high-school-stage student.
Recognize APA's own structured high-school/undergraduate research pathways as a credible official evidence channel for psychology.
Apply the achievement-tier ladder explicitly for psychology-track research: attendance/certificate is a real but lower tier than produced/presented/published output.
Do not extend the 'research requires institutional access' caution uniformly across fields — psychology-track research has a lower access barrier than lab/bench science.
Treat official UN MUN guidance (evidence-based argumentation, real-world grounding) as authoritative for distinguishing genuine engagement from surface participation.
Do not treat MUN achievement alone as sufficient evidence for this family; pair with real-world policy/civic engagement evidence.
Do not read absence of campaign/government/NGO internship evidence as a motivation gap without considering geographic access.
There is no required or specifically-rewarded 'pre-law' major; do not imply one exists.
Recommend broad skill-building across multiple possible majors rather than narrowing a law-interested student's academic path.
Surface court observation as a comparatively low-access-barrier evidence channel for this family, distinct from more consistently access-gated internships.
Treat National History Day as a strong, officially-structured evidence source for the history sub-family, with its own clean achievement-tier progression.
Treat National High School Ethics Bowl as a legitimate, distinct-format (collaborative reasoning, not adversarial debate) evidence source for philosophy/ethics.
For journalism-track evidence, favor a small number of substantive edited/reported pieces over volume; adapt the professional-publication bar down for high-school stage.
Treat Scholastic Art & Writing Awards as a well-established tiered evidence channel; non-medaling submission is still real evidence of sustained craft given the large applicant pool.
Treat architecture/design evidence as portfolio-and-process-centered; process documentation is legitimate evidence on par with finished pieces.
Do not assume a thin design portfolio reflects an access barrier the way a paid program would — core evidence (sketching, self-directed design work) is broadly accessible.
Treat National Portfolio Day's standard guidance as the reference model for visual-art evidence expectations.
Never suggest production value/equipment quality is a priority evidence gap for film/media work; storytelling, composition, and editing are what reviewers name as differentiating.
The tier-aware redundancy model is honestly executable only for the research dimension today (via output_type); treat it as aspirational elsewhere until more evidence-state data exists.
Do not assume US-style curriculum-context admissions mechanisms exist, or don't exist, in non-US systems without verifying per-system.
Before treating a country/curriculum gap as unowned, check whether another concurrent research lane already covers it.
Recognize paid part-time work as legitimate career_exploration/professional-exposure evidence on par with an internship.

[SESSION-LOCAL NUMBERING — COLLIDES WITH PEER's RULE-COUNSEL-056, NOT YET RECONCILED] Exempt career_exploration/intellectual_curiosity candidates from redundancy/saturation discounting for Phase-1 (exploration-stage) students.

Turkish YKS-track admission is exam-score-dominated; extracurricular/development-dimension counseling should not be presented as admissions-strategically important for this pathway the way it would be for US holistic review.
rules.note: Upgraded from medium-high on a follow-up pass — the peer session's direct ÖSYM domain fetch plus convergent YKS-calculator cross-check corroborates and sharpens rather than weakens the claim; see RULE-COUNSEL-109 for the specific OBP-channel finding.

rules.statement: UK UCAS applications reward subject-relevant ('super-curricular') evidence far more heavily than generic extracurricular breadth for competitive courses.
rules.note: Upgraded from medium-high on a follow-up pass — the peer session directly fetched UCAS's own official advice pages and confirmed the claim verbatim rather than via secondary paraphrase.

rules.statement: This package's 9-dimension taxonomy and redundancy findings should be treated as general student-development guidance, not assumed to transfer directly as admissions-strategy guidance outside US-style holistic-review systems.
Building a geography/admissions-system-conditional weighting layer above the development taxonomy is the single highest-leverage next research task arising from this package.
France's Parcoursup dossier includes activity/motivation elements weighted by program selectivity; Tier 2 — meaningfully lighter-touch than the US, heavier than Germany/Switzerland.
Germany's admission is Abitur-grade/NC-driven with a large open-admission (zulassungsfrei) category and no general extracurricular-activity factor for the standard domestic pathway.
rules.note: Mechanism upgraded to official-source (DAAD) confidence on a follow-up pass; national prevalence percentage remains genuinely unpublished, not merely unresearched.

rules.statement: Dutch admission is diploma-based/open for most programs; numerus fixus decentralized selection generally does not emphasize extracurricular activities specifically.
rules.note: Mechanism (deadlines, Studiekeuzecheck, selection-step distinction) upgraded to official-source (government.nl/Studielink) confidence; the specific extracurricular-non-emphasis claim remains secondary-sourced.

rules.statement: Italian public-university restricted programs (e.g. IMAT-track medicine) are test-score-driven with no extracurricular factor; private institutions vary and may weight holistically.
rules.note: Mechanism (MUR as administering ministry) upgraded to official-source confidence on a follow-up pass.

rules.statement: Swiss admission is Matura pass/fail-gated for nearly all programs (including ETH/EPFL) with no activity review; medicine's sole exception is a separate aptitude test, not an activity portfolio.
Frame recommendations differently by target-system tier: 'strengthens your application' for Tier 1/2 targets, 'supports your development / matters for a named alternative pathway' for Tier 3 targets.
For a Tier-3-track student, prioritize academic/exam-preparation recommendations as the primary admissions-relevant lever, without implying the other 8 dimensions stop mattering for development.
Key the tier conditional off the student's stated target institution/system, never off nationality, residence, or curriculum alone.

Treat 'rising junior/senior' (roughly grade 11 application, grade 12 program) as a well-evidenced eligibility pattern for flagship structured research programs; a younger student's absence of this evidence type is expected, not a gap.

Evaluate redundancy by whether scope/responsibility escalated across years, not by whether the student stayed in the same organization or switched — same-organization stagnation is the actual redundant pattern, not repetition itself.
Not every pathway's escalation stage requires an external gated program; self-directed curation/narrowing is a legitimate escalation mechanism for portfolio-based creative fields.

For a student discovering an interest late relative to a pathway's typical timeline, recommend a compressed depth-first pathway sized to remaining time; never recommend retroactively demonstrating skipped early-pathway stages.

Ontario's general-case admission is a computed grade average against a published threshold; holistic supplementary applications are real but concentrated in a specifically-named subset of competitive programs, not universal.
rules.note: Revised on a follow-up pass from an earlier, less precise 'Tier 2, closer to UK' framing — see RULE-COUNSEL-082.

rules.statement: Spain's EBAU/Selectividad is Tier 3 (60% grades + 40% national exam, explicitly no extracurricular weight).
rules.note: Mechanism (60/40 weighting) upgraded to official-source (La Moncloa + Ministry of Education) confidence on a follow-up pass.

rules.statement: For an unresearched European country, default to a Tier-3 assumption until specifically verified otherwise, based on a 7-country sample where 5 of 7 were Tier 3; present as a probabilistic default, not a fact about that specific country.
Prioritize geography-tier recommendation weighting first among this package's proposals — highest impact, needs no new data collection, uses data already collected at onboarding.
Prefer a specific target university's own country over a student's general target_geographies selection when both are available.
Ship the simple, self-reported achievement-tier field before attempting the harder structural application-to-outcome linkage.

Real admissions systems (Common App's Additional Information / Challenges and Circumstances sections) officially expect health/disability context for gapped profiles — direct precedent, not an invented consideration.

Chronic health conditions are common enough (~23-30% and rising per peer-reviewed data, higher under broader definitions) to treat as a standing, not edge-case, possible explanation for a thin profile.
rules.note: Corrected upward on a follow-up pass — original figure (~15-20%, SRC-CS-038) understated actual prevalence; peer-reviewed longitudinal data used instead.

rules.statement: Never collect, prompt for, or store health/disability or caregiving-responsibility information; only read and respect voluntarily-disclosed context in existing free-text fields, never infer from its absence.

Canada's general case is Tier 3 (grade-formula-driven) with a Tier-1/2-like holistic layer only for a specifically-named subset of competitive programs — closer to Turkey/Germany's narrow aptitude-quota exceptions than to the UK's broader super-curricular weighting.

İŞKUR's official Future Occupations list includes several medicine/clinical roles (Doktor, Hemşire, Fizyoterapist, Ergoterapist, Dil ve Konuşma Terapisti) — career-outlook signal only, not admissions-evidence guidance.
İŞKUR's list includes Psikolog and Özel Eğitim Öğretmeni — career-outlook signal only.
İŞKUR's list includes Avukat (Lawyer) — career-outlook signal only.
İŞKUR's list includes Mimar, İç Mimar, Tasarım, and Modelist — the strongest match of any family checked against this source; career-outlook signal only.
Prefer UK National Careers Service job profiles over BLS/O*NET for a UK-facing medicine-track student.
Prefer UK NCS job profiles (Clinical/Forensic Psychologist) over BLS/O*NET for a UK-facing psychology-track student.
For a UK-facing law-interested student, name the solicitor/barrister split explicitly since qualification pathways differ by branch.
For a UK/EU-facing architecture student, name that 'architect' is a legally regulated title, distinct from this document's general portfolio-evidence framing.

IB's CAS core component is a real, officially-documented, curriculum-mandated structured-engagement requirement (~3-4 hrs/week over 18 months); check for it before treating an IB student's non-CAS activity list as thin.
Generalize the curriculum-mandated-structure caution beyond IB to any curriculum with significant known structured/co-curricular expectations.

The signal-quality-to-evaluators redundancy justification does not apply for Tier-3-track targets with no application file; only opportunity-cost survives there — condition redundancy guidance on target-tier.
Treat 'social work' as spanning genuinely distinct subfields (clinical, macro/community, medical, school, child welfare); probe which before assuming evidence relevance.
Recognize emotional resilience as a load-bearing, not secondary, skill for social work specifically, per BLS's own framing.
Distinguish sustained, casework-adjacent volunteering from generic episodic volunteering when evaluating social-work-track evidence.
US clinical social work licensure requires a CSWE-accredited MSW plus supervised post-graduate clinical hours and a licensing exam, state-specific in details.
UK social work practice requires Social Work England registration (or devolved-nation equivalent) after an approved qualification.
Turkey's 'sosyal çalışmacı' title is officially bachelor's-degree-specific — confirmed via primary regulation text (MEB Art. 3(p)), fetched by the peer session.
rules.note: Upgraded from secondary to primary source on a follow-up pass; see RULE-COUNSEL-107 for the part of the original claim that was NOT confirmed and was downgraded.

rules.statement: State the general 'degree + separate registration/title-control step' pattern to students while being explicit mechanics are country-specific — mirrors 18-education-teaching.md's own finding, suggesting a broader pattern across regulated-title professions.

A country's general admissions tier assignment must always be checked against the specific target field — even a predominantly Tier-3 country can have named fields (e.g. Turkish state conservatory admission) with a genuine audition/aptitude exception.
rules.note: Cross-branch finding: verified by the peer session against official Turkish conservatory-admission guidance (their RULE-COUNSEL-238, 06-major-family-evidence/20-performing-arts-music.md), folded into this branch's doc11 directly rather than left only on peer's side. Not independently re-verified by this session against the primary source.

rules.statement: When a country/target-tier exception applies, a deep single-domain profile that would read as thin under a naive blanket-tier read is instead exactly the right evidence shape for the exception itself.

Germany's medical-licensure model (Medizinstudium + state medical examination, commonly called the Staatsexamen though that is not the Approbationsordnung's own term + Approbation, protected Arzt/Ärztin title) is a genuinely distinct, longer, more exam-heavy model than the UK's.
rules.note: Upgraded from medium-high on a follow-up pass -- Bundesaerztekammer's own page directly confirms the Approbation requirement; also found the regulation's own term is 'Aerztliche Pruefung,' not 'Staatsexamen,' a precision correction to this rule's own phrasing.

rules.statement: For a German-track law student, sharpen the 'no required pre-law major' finding: German legal training is a single, unified pathway (5-year Jurastudium/Erste Pruefung, then a 2-year Referendariat, then the Zweite Staatsexamen, BRAK's own page giving ~9 years total) with no US-style flexible major-then-law-school equivalent.
rules.note: Upgraded from medium-high on a follow-up pass -- directly fetched and quoted BRAK's own student-facing page, sharpening the '7-11 years' range to BRAK's own stated ~9-year figure.

rules.statement: Germany requires Approbation (same mechanism as medicine) for clinical/therapeutic psychology practice specifically, under the Psychotherapeutengesetz — a legal, not just practical, distinction between clinical and non-clinical psychology tracks.
rules.note: Upgraded from medium-high on a follow-up pass -- directly fetched and quoted the Federal Ministry of Health's (BMG) own page, resolving the source's previously-flagged 'no consolidated federal ministry statement' limitation.

rules.statement: Germany title-protects 'Architekt' via a chamber-based, state-by-state system (16 regional Architektenkammer under the federal Bundesarchitektenkammer) — same protection concept as UK's ARB, more fragmented administration.

The claim that Turkish associate-degree graduates receive a different, narrower social-work title is NOT confirmed by the one primary regulation checked (silent on associate-degree titling) — downgraded to secondary-source-only confidence rather than left at its original higher rating.
rules.note: A primary-source check should sharpen AND narrow a claim, not blanket-validate everything asserted alongside the confirmed part — this rule is that discipline applied to this package's own prior claim.

rules.statement: Turkey's MEB Rehberlik Hizmetleri Yönetmeliği, Article 3(i), formally defines 'Psikolog' as requiring bachelor's-level psychology education.

YKS placement score has exactly one non-exam channel (OBP, diploma-grade-derived, roughly 250-500 raw range weighted at 0.12x, halved to 0.06x for a previously-placed candidate) — itself purely academics-dimension and small relative to the overall score (capped around 60 points out of a total running into the hundreds), providing zero channel for leadership/community_impact/entrepreneurship/research/awards_distinction regardless of how that channel is weighted.
rules.note: Sharpens RULE-COUNSEL-057 rather than qualifying it — found by the peer session via direct ÖSYM domain fetch plus convergent independent YKS-calculator cross-check, reported to and incorporated by this session.

rules.statement: Canada's named 'holistic supplementary application' competitive programs are not one uniform mechanism: Waterloo Engineering's AIF explicitly invites activity/accomplishment description, while Queen's Commerce and McMaster Health Sciences score written/video responses to structured reflective prompts with no activities-list criterion in their own published rubrics. Never assume 'holistic supplementary application' means the same evaluation mechanism across different named programs without checking each program's own rubric.

For a Queen's-Commerce- or McMaster-HHSP-track student specifically, never phrase supplementary-application advice as 'add more activities to your profile' — by these programs' own published rubrics, the scored lever is reflective-response quality on specific prompts, not activity-list breadth.
rules.note: Direct consequence of RULE-COUNSEL-110's primary-source finding.

rules.statement: This package's earlier characterization of the University of Toronto as running an explicitly holistic process weighing leadership/community involvement/extracurricular activities for its general admissions process is not confirmed by UofT's own official assessment page, which instead describes a grade/prerequisite-driven general process with program-specific (not universal) supplemental requirements. The original claim is withdrawn for UofT's general process, not merely qualified.
rules.note: A primary-source check that corrected rather than merely sharpened a prior medium-confidence secondary claim — see RULE-COUNSEL-107 for the same discipline applied previously to a social-work claim.

rules.statement: For a UK-track target, weight subject-relevant intellectual_curiosity/research/execution_project_depth/awards_distinction high and their non-subject-relevant counterparts low; weight leadership low-medium regardless of subject-relevance; weight community_impact low except for medicine.
rules.note: Directionally sourced via RULE-COUNSEL-058 (official UCAS guidance); the specific per-dimension ordinal calls are this document's own reasoned extension, not independently verified dimension-by-dimension against UCAS guidance.

rules.statement: For a France/Parcoursup-track target: academics maps to the 'Résultats académiques'/'Compétences académiques' champs (high-weighted); intellectual_curiosity maps to 'Savoir-être' (curiosité intellectuelle, ouverture au monde) and subject-specific 'Motivation'; leadership/community_impact map to the 'Engagements, activités' champ (school-council engagement, civic service named explicitly). All 5 champs are mandatorily percentage-weighted per formation summing to 100%, but any single formation's exact percentage per champ is formation-specific, not general knowledge.
rules.note: Originally marked fully unresolved (no per-dimension sourcing); substantially resolved on a follow-up pass after directly reading DGESIP's official CGEV framework document. See RULE-COUNSEL-117 for the underlying source finding.

rules.statement: Tier alone is insufficient for Tier-3-with-named-carve-out targets; ORYN's counselor must know the specific named program and what that program's own rubric scores before recommending anything, since carve-out mechanisms range from activity-description to pure reflective-response scoring to skills auditions to standardized aptitude tests.
rules.note: Direct consequence of RULE-COUNSEL-110's primary-source finding.

rules.statement: Country/tier-level conditioning and field-level (major-family) conditioning must compose together; medicine alone demonstrates the 'exception direction' flips by country (activity-rewarding in US/UK, aptitude-test-gated in Switzerland, more-exam-dominated-than-usual in Turkey), so neither level of conditioning is sufficient alone.
rules.note: High confidence for the medicine cases specifically (each individually sourced elsewhere in this package: RULE-COUNSEL-032/033/058/065/057/103); medium for how broadly this generalizes to fields beyond medicine, which this document did not check.

rules.statement: France's Parcoursup applications are evaluated against exactly 5 nationally-defined evaluation fields (academic results, academic competencies/methodology, soft skills, motivation/program-fit, activities/engagement), each mandatorily assigned a formation-specific percentage weight summing to 100%, per DGESIP's official CGEV framework document. Confirms activities/engagement is a real, structurally-guaranteed evaluation category, not optional or vague.
rules.note: Official DGESIP document, directly extracted via pypdf after WebFetch's own extractor failed on this file.

rules.statement: ORYN's recommendation vocabulary has no category for 'practice articulating existing experience in a specific structured format' (e.g. rehearsing a reflective response to Queen's-Commerce-style prompts), as distinct from 'go get more/better experience' -- the entire achievement-tier evidence model is built around logged achievements, not response-rehearsal preparation.
rules.note: A real gap this persona's own walkthrough demonstrates the current model cannot cleanly express, not a hypothetical concern.

rules.statement: Per-target explanations for a shared recommended action must name the mechanism by which each target values it (direct scored evidence vs. indirect raw material for a differently-scored assessment), not only the framing register -- a blended or mechanism-silent explanation risks a student over-investing in the wrong kind of preparation for at least one target, even when the recommended action is correctly the same for both.
rules.note: Direct consequence of Persona J's walkthrough; sharpens RULE-COUNSEL-066 rather than replacing it.

rules.statement: ORYN's evidence/recommendation model needs to distinguish at least three structurally different non-academic assessment types: achievement-evidence-based (US/UK/Waterloo), institution-authored reflective response (Queen's Commerce/McMaster HHSP), and standardized third-party situational-judgment testing (CASPer -- 500+ programs, medicine/health-sciences/PA/nursing/dental-hygiene currently, expanding into education/business/engineering). Each needs different preparation guidance.
rules.note: Found by checking whether Persona J's gap (RULE-COUNSEL-118) generalizes beyond Queen's/McMaster specifically -- it does, and further than expected.

rules.statement: UK medicine/dentistry admission is a compound case, not just grades plus holistic clinical-exposure evidence: 57 UK universities also require the UCAT, which includes a separately-banded Situational Judgement Test subtest -- not activity-based at all. Confirms RULE-COUNSEL-120's 'standardized third-party situational-judgment testing' category generalizes beyond CASPer/North America as a recurring structural type (different specific instruments per region), not a single tool.
rules.note: Checked directly after RULE-COUNSEL-120 raised the question of how far the typology generalizes; UCAT confirms it's a real category, not a CASPer-specific quirk.

rules.statement: Ireland's CAO system is Tier 3 (Leaving Certificate points, no general activity weight, confirmed via CAO's own official page) with medicine as a named exception in the aptitude-test direction (HPAT, a 117-question multiple-choice test including a 40%-weighted 'Understanding People' interpersonal-judgment section) -- the same structural pattern as the UK's UCAT, a second country confirming RULE-COUNSEL-121 generalizes.
rules.note: Extends the generic-Europe-fallback sample from 7 to 8 countries (see RULE-COUNSEL-075's updated count) and finds a second UCAT-shaped medicine exception, suggesting this may be a recurring pattern worth checking whenever a new country is researched.

rules.statement: DECA's own official competitive-events page names specific, distinct entrepreneurship events (Start-Up Business Plan, Independent Business Plan, Franchise Business Plan, International Business Plan, Innovation Plan, Entrepreneurship Series) rather than one generic 'business competition' -- gives Pathway 2 the same named-program evidence-tier hook Pathways 1 and 3 already had.
